topic: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Guide: Deploy Production AI Agents on AWS

key_points: AWS launch narrative: AgentCore moves agentic apps from prototype to production with managed runtime, memory, identity, gateway, browser, code interpreter, and observability.
Important update: AgentCore became generally available on October 13, 2025, and GA added VPC, AWS PrivateLink, CloudFormation, and resource tagging across AgentCore services.
Positions AgentCore around production constraints: secure tool/data access, scale, governance, and monitoring.
Official docs define AgentCore as an agentic platform for building, deploying, and operating agents securely at scale using any framework and foundation model.
Highlights framework support for CrewAI, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, and Strands Agents, which is crucial for comparison against Bedrock Agents and open-source runtimes.
Breaks down modular services: Runtime, Memory, Identity, Gateway, Observability, Browser, Code Interpreter, Evaluations, Policy, Registry, Optimization, and Payments.
SEO-focused 2026 guide emphasizes the production gap: failed AI PoCs, missing observability, security gaps, memory, and scaling issues.
Compares AgentCore with Google ADK and open-source frameworks, arguing AWS wins on production runtime, CloudWatch traces, managed memory, and IAM integration.
Uses enterprise case-study style examples and claims faster deployment/insights; writer should treat vendor claims cautiously and prefer AWS primary sources for facts.

Practitioner operations guide aimed at engineers hardening AgentCore beyond PoC: observability, cost optimization, failure modes, resilience, capacity planning, security, deployment strategy, and incident response.
Strong production angle: four-signal observability model, CloudWatch Transaction Search setup, traces/logs/metrics/evaluations, runbooks, blue-green/canary/shadow deployments.
Useful gap to exploit: combine beginner concepts and production operations in one guide rather than splitting into a long series.
Practitioner guide explains how AgentCore evolved from preview in July 2025 to GA in October 2025 and expanded in December 2025.
Focuses on when to use Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, and regional routing in real AWS builds.
Good competitive benchmark for tone: practical, opinionated, build-focused rather than marketing-heavy.

stats.fact: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore became generally available on October 13, 2025.
At GA, all AgentCore services gained support for VPC, AWS PrivateLink, AWS CloudFormation, and resource tagging.
Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore became generally available on March 3, 2026 in 13 AWS Regions.
AgentCore Runtime, Browser, and Code Interpreter are priced at $0.0895 per vCPU-hour and $0.00945 per GB-hour under active-consumption pricing.
AgentCore Gateway pricing is $0.005 per 1,000 API invocations, $0.025 per 1,000 Search API invocations, and $0.02 per 100 tools indexed per month.
AgentCore Memory pricing includes $0.25 per 1,000 short-term memory events, $0.75 per 1,000 long-term memory records stored per month with built-in strategies, and $0.50 per 1,000 memory retrievals.
AWS pricing examples estimate 10 million monthly customer-support Runtime sessions at $7,235 when sessions run 60 seconds with 70% I/O wait, because CPU billing excludes idle I/O wait time.
AWS says AgentCore Evaluations includes 13 built-in evaluators for common quality dimensions and supports CI/CD thresholds plus production sampling.
The global agentic AI market was valued at $7.29 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow from $9.14 billion in 2026 to $139.19 billion by 2034 at a 40.50% CAGR.
Fortune Business Insights cites Capgemini data that 14% of organizations have deployed AI agents, 23% have pilots, and 61% are exploring or preparing for AI agent deployment.

angles: Frame AgentCore as the AWS production layer for agents, not just another agent framework: it solves runtime isolation, tool governance, memory, identity, evaluation, and observability.
Clarify Bedrock Agents vs AgentCore early: Bedrock Agents is faster/no-code for standard Bedrock-native agents; AgentCore is code-first, framework-agnostic, and production-oriented.
Give a deployment path: local framework agent -> AgentCore Runtime -> Gateway/Identity -> Memory -> Observability/Evaluations -> Policy -> cost controls.
Add a cost model section that separates foundation model token cost from AgentCore platform cost, then explains active resource billing and why I/O wait matters.
Treat governance as the differentiator for enterprise readers: Policy outside agent code, Cedar conversion from natural language, Gateway interception, and CloudWatch auditability.
Include production-readiness checklist: VPC/PrivateLink, IAM least privilege, per-session isolation, retries/timeouts, evaluation gates, runbooks, alarms, and canary or shadow rollout.
Cover new 2026 capabilities: Policy GA, episodic memory, Evaluations, Optimization preview, Registry preview, and Payments preview.
Warn about lock-in and complexity: AgentCore is strongest for AWS-heavy teams but overkill for simple prototypes or teams needing cloud-neutral orchestration.
